newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Turner painting stolen in Australia worth $3 million.
newsitem.headline: Turner painting stolen in Australia worth $3 million.

text.p: An oil painting by English master William Turner has been stolen from a Sydney home and could be worth up to A$4 million (US$3.2 million), police said on Friday.

The 75 cm by 100 cm (30 by 40 inch) Turner painting, titled "Royal Barge on Stormy Seas", was among 10 paintings and two rare books stolen from a private home in the exclusive northern suburb of Killara on December 28.
A police spokesman said the announcement of the theft had been delayed because the family which owned the painting had been seeking independent valuations.
The painting had been insured for just A$350,000, police said.
"It now seems it could be worth as much as two million pounds (A$4 million)," the spokesman said.
The discrepancy between the painting's insured value and its actual worth was because the work was a family heirloom and had never been valued in Europe, police said.
The thief disarmed an elaborate alarm system to enter the home while its owners were away on holiday.
The spokesman added that it was unlikely the painting was still in Australia and said international police and art galleries had been notified of the theft.
The nine other paintings stolen included works by acclaimed Australian artist Sydney Nolan. The books were Hebrew and Latin texts printed on hemp in 1626 and bound in pig skin.
Turner, who died in 1851, produced about 500 oil paintings and 2,000 water colours.
The highest price paid for a Turner oil was 11 million pounds (US$17.7 million) in 1993.
